stake_L1_drift_bar_as_a_fraction_of_the_.name: L1 drift bar as a fraction of the thermostat's posted work
stake_L1_drift_bar_as_a_fraction_of_the_.arithmetic: LIQUID-1's own arm: drift_peak / |work_thermostat| = 1.076398662e-5 / 7.669546662e-1. The bar on any arm is this fraction times THAT arm's own posted thermostat work, so LIQUID-1 sits exactly on the bar and LIQUID-2 is asked to be no worse per unit of work pumped. FENCE: drift_peak is an extremum and the thermostat column accumulates, so this ratio loosens with arm length; the screen's arms are all the same length for that reason and the counted arm's length is reported beside it.

stake_R3_crossover_implied_by_LIQUID-1's.name: R3 crossover implied by LIQUID-1's measured MSD exponent, fs
stake_R3_crossover_implied_by_LIQUID-1's.arithmetic: two powers joined continuously (ballistic t^2 below t_c, diffusive t_c*t above): a log-log slope over [t1, t2] is alpha = 1 + ln(t_c/t1)/ln(t2/t1), so t_c = t1 * (t2/t1)^(alpha-1). LIQUID-1's window is its own lag ladder (2 .. 210 of its readout stride = counted_frames_run / readouts) times the tables' step measured again here.

inputs.field: refusal (the MSD exponent, parsed from the lens's own sentence)

stake_R3_price_ceiling,_seconds.name: R3 price ceiling, seconds
stake_R3_price_ceiling,_seconds.arithmetic: ten times LIQUID-1's own counted arm (l2.wall_seconds), which is the upper edge of the band that arm priced itself in. A counted arm over this is VOID BY PRICE and R3 with it.

stake_S:_the_Erdos-Renyi_giant_component.name: S: the Erdos-Renyi giant component at LIQUID-1's own measured degree
stake_S:_the_Erdos-Renyi_giant_component.arithmetic: mean degree z = 2 * hbonds_per_molecule (the lens counts each bond once; a degree counts it at both ends), then the fixed point of s = 1 - exp(-z s). This is what a RANDOM graph of the same density would give, and it is the reference the measured largest component is read against.
